questions.question: Dussehra is celebrated in ________ month of the Hindu calendar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dussehra** is celebrated in the Hindu month of **Ashvina**.
 
• Ashvina usually falls in the months of **September and October** in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Dussehra marks the end of the nine-day festival of **Navratri** and the victory of Lord Rama over the demon king **Ravana**.
 
• It symbolizes the triumph of good over evil and is celebrated with great enthusiasm across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navratri** is a major Hindu festival that spans nine nights and is celebrated every year in the autumn.
 
• The festival is associated with the prominent battle that took place between **Durga** and the demon **Mahishasura** and celebrates the victory of Good over Evil.
 
• Different regions of India celebrate Navratri in different ways, with **Garba** and **Dandiya** being popular in Gujarat and **Durga Puja** being a major celebration in West Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is observed by the tribal people of Jharkhand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Bhagta Parab.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• This jubilee comes between the period of spring and summer.
 
• Among the ethnical people of Jharkhand, Bhagta Parab is best known as the deification of Budha Baba.
 
• People gormandize during the day and carry the bathing Pahan the clerk, to the ethnical mandir called Sarana Mandir.
 
• The Pahan occasionally called Laya, gets out of the pond, the addicts make a chain, locking their shanks with each other, and come forward to offer their bare casket to Laya for a walkover.
 
• After deification in the evening, addicts take part in dynamic and vigorous Chhau cotillion with lots of gymnastic conduct and masks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nongkrem**:

 
 
• The Nongkrem dance festival is celebrated during Autumn at Smit, the cultural center of the Khasi Hills.
 
• A five-day-long religious festival of the Khasis, Ka Pomblang Nongkrem dance is popularly known as the Nongkrem dance.
 
 
 
• **Losar:**
 
 
• The Tibetan word “ Losar ”, which translates to “ New Year ” in English is the most popular and significant jubilee of the North East Indian state of Sikkim and is celebrated with great enthusiasm every time.
 
• The history of the Losar festival predates the arrival of Buddhism in Tibet and its neighboring regions like parts of India, Bhutan, and Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Suata**:
 
 
• Like the Ghadalya festival of Malwa, the Suata festival is famous in the Bundelkhand region.
 
• In this festival an ornate statue of the demon is installed on the wall and in the upper part of it, a statue of ShivaParvati is placed, the sun and moon are made on the wall, then the young women worship and sing.

questions.question: Ugadi is a ________ New Year celebrated in the month of March.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Telugu.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, **Ugadi or Yugadi **is the **Hindu New Year's Day**, which is observed in the Indian states of** Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.**
 
• On the** first day of the Hindu lunisolar calendar month of Chaitra, it is celebrated festively in these areas. **
 
• The Pachadi is a popular festive dish that incorporates a wide range of flavours, including sweet, sour, salty, bitter, astringent, and spicy.
 
• It is a symbolic reminder in **Telugu and Kannada Hindu traditions** that one should expect a wide range of experiences in the approaching new year and make the most of them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gudi Padwa- Marathi New Year**.

 
 
• Gudi Padwa is a spring festival that marks the New Year celebration for Marathi Hindus. It is celebrated on the first day of the Chaitra month according to the lunisolar Hindu calendar in Maharashtra and Konkan regions.
 
 
 
• **Poila Baisakh - The Bengali New Year**
 
 
• It is also known as Poila Baisakh or Bangla Noboborsho. It is Celebrated in the month of April throughout West Bengal, Assam, Tripura, and in the neighbouring country i.e. Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Baisakhi also marks the Punjabi New Year.**
 
 
• According to the English calendar, the date of Baisakhi corresponds to April 13 every year and April 14 once every 36 years. This variation is due to the festival being observed as per the Indian solar calendar.

questions.question: Which of the following cultural festivals of South India is associated with the folklore of King Mahabali?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Onam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Onam,** the vibrant cultural festival celebrated in **South India**, holds deep roots in the legend of **King Mahabali.**
 
• According to local folklore, Kerala was once under the rule of the **benevolent Asura (demon) king**, Mahabali, also affectionately known as Maveli or Onathappan.
 
• Despite his demon status, Mahabali was revered for his unparalleled generosity and compassion. His reign was hailed as a golden era marked by joy, harmony, and abundance.
 
• Each year, during the** ten-day Onam festivities,** the people of Kerala eagerly anticipate the symbolic return of their beloved king.
 
• The poignant folk song **"Maveli nadu vaneedum kalam"** poignantly recounts Mahabali's selfless sacrifice and resonates deeply with the spirit of Onam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gudi Padwa,** also referred to as the Marathi New Year or Hindu New Year, is a festive occasion primarily celebrated by Marathi and Konkani Hindus. It is observed in regions such as Maharashtra, Goa, and Daman. The term "Gudi" symbolizes a flag, while "Padwa" denotes the first day of the lunar fortnight.
 
• **Ugadi,** alternatively known as Yugadi, is a significant Hindu festival marking the commencement of the New Year. It is predominantly celebrated in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka in India. The term "Ugadi" originates from the Sanskrit words "yuga" (age) and "adi" (beginning), symbolizing the onset of a new age or era.
 
• **Pongal** holds immense importance among Tamil people in Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka, and the global Tamil diaspora. Celebrated over three or four days, each day of Pongal is marked by distinct rituals. The four consecutive days are Bhogi, Surya Pongal, Mattu Pongal, and Kanum Pongal. This festival venerates Surya, the solar deity in Hinduism, and aligns with the occasion of Makar Sankranti.

questions.question: Which festival comes at the end of Navratri and Durga Pooja?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dussehra.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dussehra marks the victory of Lord Rama over the demon king Ravana, symbolizing the **triumph** of **good** over **evil.**
 
• It is celebrated with the burning of effigies of Ravana, Meghnath, and Kumbhakarna in many parts of India, especially in the northern regions.
 
• **Relation to Navratri:** It is observed on the **10th day (Vijayadashami)** of the Hindu festival of Navratri, following nine days of worshipping Goddess Durga.
 
• **Regional Variations: **While predominantly a North Indian festival, Dussehra has variations across India, such as the **Mysore Dasara** in Karnataka and **Ramlila performances** in North India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Christmas:**

 
 
• Christmas is celebrated annually on** December 25th**, marking the birth of **Jesus Christ.**
 
• **Global Significance:** It is a major Christian festival celebrated globally with traditions like exchanging gifts, decorating Christmas trees, and attending church services.
 
• Christmas is recognized as a **public holiday** in many countries, including India, where it is celebrated by various communities.
 
 
 
• **Pongal:**
 
 
• Pongal is a major** harvest festival **celebrated in Tamil Nadu, usually in mid-January, marking the end of the winter solstice.
 
• **Multi-Day Event:** It is a four-day festival with each day having its significance, starting with **Bhogi** and ending with** Kaanum** Pongal.
 
• Cultural Importance: Pongal is a thanksgiving to nature, particularly the** Sun God**, for agricultural abundance.
 
 
 
• **Holi:**
 
 
• Holi, also known as the **Festival of Colors**, is celebrated primarily in March, signifying the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil.
 
• **Mythological Significance:** It is linked to the legend of Prahlad and Holika, where Prahlad’s devotion to Lord Vishnu led to the defeat of the demoness Holika.
 
• **Social Significance:** Holi is known for breaking social barriers, as people come together to play with colors and share sweets, promoting harmony.

questions.question: Chad Sukra festival is celebrated by the Jaintia tribe of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Chad Sukra festival** is celebrated by the **Jaintia tribe of Meghalaya, **also known as the **Pnar people, every year in April.**
 
• The festival honors the start of the sowing season and is also a way to ask for protection from natural calamities that could harm crops.
 
• The festival dates back to the **Jaintia Kingdom**, when the king would move his court from **Sutnga to Jaintiapur,** and people from all over the kingdom would perform for him and his ministers at the start of spring.
 
• The word Chad Sukra literally means "dance with a joyful heart, with health and vitality".
 
• During the festival, farmers offer prayers to mother earth and thank her for her blessings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In addition to rituals and prayers, the Chad Sukra festival features traditional dances, including the **"Laho" dance.**
 
• In this dance, two young men flank a girl, linking arms with her, and they dance together in synchronized steps.
 
• Women participating in the festival adorn themselves in traditional attire such as ryndia stem, thoh saru, khyrwang, sapjat, kein shrooh/kyrshah, while men wear iuslein pyniein, iuspong, ryndia tlem, among others.
 
• Furthermore, women embellish their attire with ornaments like paila, khoila (earrings), and khadu (bracelets), adding to the festive atmosphere of the occasion.

questions.question: Maimata is a popular folk dance of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tripura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mamita Festival **in **Tripura, India,** it's typically associated with the **Tripuri community** rather than the Kaloi community.
 
• The Mamita Festival is indeed a harvest festival celebrated by the Tripuri people, and Maimata is an integral part of the festivities.
 
• Hojagiri, on the other hand, is another** fascinating folk dance of Tripura, **primarily performed by women during the Hojagiri festivals.
 
• This dance form involves balancing a bottle or pitcher on the head while executing graceful movements and intricate footwork.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tripura, **situated in Northeast India, ranks as the** country's third-smallest state, **covering an area of 10,491 square kilometers (4,051 square miles).
 
• Despite its small size, it is the seventh-least populous state, with a population of 3.67 million.
 
• Bordered by Assam and Mizoram to the east and Bangladesh to the north, south, and west, Tripura comprises 8 districts and 23 sub-divisions.
 
• Its capital, Agartala, serves as both the administrative center and the largest city in the state. With 19 distinct tribal communities coexisting alongside a predominantly Bengali population, Tripura boasts a diverse cultural landscape. The state recognizes Bengali, English, and Kokborok as its official languages.
 
• Historically, the region formed part of the Tripuri Kingdom, governed for centuries by the Manikya Dynasty. Under British colonial rule, it became a princely state and later acceded to independent India in 1947.
 
• Initially categorized as a 'Part C State' (union territory), Tripura attained full statehood in **1972**.

questions.question: Nauroz is celebrated by which of the following communities in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parsi.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Navroz is the Iranian New Year**, which is widely known as the **Persian New Year **is celebrated worldwide by some religious groups.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the **first of Farvardin - Zoroastrian calendar’s first month **and the onset of spring.
 
• **Listed in UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity of India.**
 
• The festival is also known as Nowrouz, Navruz, Nauroz, Novruz, Nevruz, and Nowruz.
 
• The festival commences at the vernal equinox stroke, the time when the sun passes through the equator. This year, it falls on **March 21**.
 
• Although the date of the Navroz Festival falls in March worldwide, India celebrates it in August as well. The second date of the Navroz Festival is calculated according to the Shahen Shahi calendar, which is 17th August.
 
• It is celebrated in Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, India, Iran, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. In India, it is mostly celebrated in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parsis follow the Zoroastrian faith**, which emphasizes the worship of **Ahura Mazda**, the supreme deity, and promotes principles of good thoughts, good words, and good deeds.
 
• Prominent Parsi figures include **industrialist Jamsetji Tata, nuclear physicist Homi Bhabha, and musician Zubin Mehta.**

questions.question: Which festival is popularly known as the festival of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwali**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diwali** is popularly known as the festival of light.
 
• It is celebrated by millions of Hindus, Sikhs, and Jains across the world.
 
• The festival signifies the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance.
 
• During Diwali, homes, shops, and public places are decorated with small oil lamps called diyas, fireworks are set off, and sweets are shared among families and friends.
 
• The festival usually lasts five days, with the main celebrations occurring on the third day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Diwali is also known as **Deepavali**, which means "row of lights."
 
• The festival's origins can be traced back to ancient India, and it is linked to various legends, including the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after a 14-year exile and his victory over the demon king Ravana.
 
• In Jainism, Diwali marks the spiritual awakening of Lord Mahavira.
 
• Sikhs celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas, which coincides with Diwali, commemorating the release of Guru Hargobind Ji from imprisonment.
 
• Diwali is a time for cleaning and renovating homes, wearing new clothes, and performing religious rituals to invite prosperity and well-being.

questions.question: Kojagiri Poornima is a festival celebrated primarily in _______ on the full moon day of Ashwin month.

__
 
• **Kojagiri Poornima** is a festival celebrated primarily in **Maharashtra**__ on the full moon day of the Ashwin month.
 
• It is also known as **Sharad Poornima** and marks the end of the monsoon season.
 
• On this day, people stay awake all night, gazing at the moon and consuming a special preparation of milk.

• It is believed that the moon on this night is closest to the earth and its rays have healing properties.
 
• The festival has a cultural significance as it brings communities together and reinforces social bonds.

questions.question: Rongker festival is celebrated by which of the following tribes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karbi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Karbi tribe **of **Assam** celebrates the** Rongker festival**, a wintertime event filled with joy and festivities.
 
• Also known as **Dehal in Dumra Longri, **which encompasses the **Ri-Bhoi district of Meghalaya and the Kamrup Metropolitan** district of Assam, this festival holds significant cultural importance.
 
• Rongker is observed to honor local deities, revered as guardians of the community and responsible for ensuring successful crop harvests, while also serving to dispel ill fortune.
 
• Although typically celebrated on **February 5 **to coincide with the beginning of the Karbi New Year, the festival's timing may vary among different villages, depending on their preferences.
 
• Lasting for three days, the celebration is marked by various rituals and ceremonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Gond tribe**, one of India's largest indigenous communities, boasts a population exceeding 14 million individuals. They inhabit various regions across Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, and Odisha.
 
• **The Bhil tribe **constitutes a significant ethnic group in western India, contributing to the region's rich cultural diversity.
 
• Hailing from the Mokokchung District of Nagaland, India, **the Ao people** represent a prominent Naga ethnic group with a distinct cultural heritage.

questions.question: ‘Rongali Bihu’, one of the major festivals of Assam, is celebrated in the month of :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **​Rongali Bihu** is another name for **Bohag Bihu.**
 
• It is an **ethnic tradition** that is celebrated throughout **northeastern India, **including the** state of Assam.**
 
• The** Assamese indigenous ethnic tribes** commemorate it. 
 
• It marks the beginning of the** Assamese New Year.**
 
• The majority of the festival's components are of** indigenous heritage,** including** Tibetan and Tai aspects.**
 
• It usually occurs during the **second week of April,** which historically denotes the **harvest season.**
 
• It always falls on the **14th of April.**
 
• Locally, **Rongali Bihu** in Assam begins with the onset of **"Bohag."**
 
• **Bohag Bihu or Rongali Bihu, Kati Bihu or Kongali Bihu, and Magh Bihu or Bhogali Bihu **are the three main varieties of bihu.
 
• Each festival historically commemorates a **distinct paddy crop **agriculture cycle.
 
• There are seven apex periods throughout Rongali Bihu: **"Sot," "Raati," "Goru," "Manuh," "Kutum," "Mela," and "Sera."**

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated in the month of February by the Angami tribe of Nagaland?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Sekrenyi festival.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sekrenyi is celebrated annually as part of the **Mini Hornbill Tribal Festival in the month of February.**
 
• The Sekrenyi festival is the biggest festival of the Angami lineage and it falls on the 25th day of the Angami month of Kezei.
 
• It's a festivity of sanctification accompanied by feasting and singing.
 
• Locally known as** Phousanyi,** Sekrenyi of Nagaland is essentially a festival of the Angami Nagas. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Losoong Festival:**

 
 
• Losoong Festival is the Sikkimese New Year, of the Bhutia tribe, celebrated every time in the month of December.
 
• This tribe is veritably notorious in eastern India.
 
• Cham dances are performed by Buddhist Monks.
 
 
 
• **Hornbill festival:**
 
 
• The Hornbill Festival, which is called the ‘Festivals of Festivals’, is a 10-day annual cultural fest of Nagaland that showcases the rich and diverse Naga ethnicity through folk dances, traditional music, local cuisine, handicraft, art workshops, etc.
 
 
 
• **Majuli festival:**
 
 
• It is celebrated in the northeast side of the country, in the state of Assam.
 
• The place to celebrate the jubilee is the bank of River Luit, which happens to have the biggest swash islet in the world.
 
• This jubilee starts on the 21st of November each time and continues to the 24th of the same month.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated after the month of Ramzan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eid ul Fitr**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eid ul Fitr** is celebrated after the month of Ramzan (Ramadan).
 
• It is one of the most significant festivals in the Islamic calendar, marking the end of a month-long dawn-to-sunset fasting during Ramadan.
 
• The festival is also known as the "Festival of Breaking the Fast" and it is a joyous occasion for Muslims worldwide.
 
• On Eid ul Fitr, Muslims express gratitude to Allah for the strength and patience shown during Ramadan.
 
• The day begins with a special prayer called the "Salat al-Eid," which is performed in congregation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramzan (Ramadan)** is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, observed by Muslims worldwide as a month of fasting, prayer, reflection, and community.
 
• Fasting during Ramadan is one of the Five Pillars of Islam, which are the foundational acts of worship and the core beliefs of the Muslim faith.
 
• Muslims fast from dawn (Fajr) until sunset (Maghrib), abstaining from food, drink, and other physical needs to purify the soul and practice self-discipline.
 
• Eid ul Fitr is a time for Muslims to give Zakat al-Fitr (charity in the form of food) to the needy, ensuring that all Muslims can enjoy the festivities.
 
• The celebration of Eid ul Fitr varies around the world, but common practices include communal prayers, feasting, visiting friends and family, and exchanging gifts.

questions.question: Thaipusam festival is celebrated in which of the following Indian states?

questions.question: Which Goddess is associated with the Gangaur Festival celebrated in Central and Western India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goddess Parvati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goddess Parvati** is associated with the Gangaur Festival celebrated in Central and Western India.
 
• **Gangaur** is a vibrant and significant festival celebrated by the people of Rajasthan, as well as in other Indian states like Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It is dedicated to the worship of Goddess Gauri (Parvati), the consort of Lord Shiva, and is observed with great zeal and devotion during the Hindu month of Chaitra, which typically falls in March or April.
 
• The festival symbolizes various aspects including the arrival of spring, the harvest season, marital fidelity, conjugal happiness, and fertility.
 
• Women play a central role in the celebrations, offering prayers to Goddess Gauri for blessings related to marriage, marital bliss, and the well-being of their husbands. Unmarried women seek the blessings of the goddess for a suitable life partner, while married women pray for the health, longevity, and prosperity of their husbands.
 
• Gangaur is characterized by colorful processions, traditional rituals, and cultural performances that showcase the rich heritage and traditions of the region. It serves as a time for communities to come together, celebrate, and express gratitude for the blessings bestowed upon them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Parvati** is a revered Hindu goddess known for her association with the Himalayas, fertility, beauty, marriage, and the arts. She is considered one of the principal deities in Hinduism.
 
• **Saraswati** is another prominent Hindu goddess, symbolizing knowledge, music, and the arts. She is revered as the embodiment of wisdom and creativity.
 
• **Lakshmi,** often depicted as a goddess with lotus flowers, is worshipped as the deity of wealth, good fortune, happiness, youth, and beauty. She is highly esteemed in Hindu culture and is believed to bring prosperity to her devotees.
 
• **Kali **is a significant Hindu goddess associated with various aspects including time, change, creation, power, destruction, and death in the Shaktism tradition. She is often depicted as fierce and fearsome, representing the raw power of nature and the cycle of life and death.

questions.question: Goga Navami, which is primarily celebrated in the Indian state of ___________, is dedicated to the snake God, Gogaji.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goga Navami** is primarily celebrated in the Indian state of **Rajasthan**.
 
• This festival is dedicated to the snake God, **Gogaji**.
 
• Gogaji is a folk deity in Rajasthan, also revered in parts of Haryana, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• He is believed to protect his followers from snake bites and other harms.
 
• The festival involves various rituals, including processions and worship at temples dedicated to Gogaji.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gogaji is also known as **Gogaji Chauhan** and is considered a warrior-hero in Rajasthani folklore.
 
• He is often depicted riding a horse and carrying a lance.
 
• The temples dedicated to Gogaji are known as **Gogamedi**, where devotees gather in large numbers during the festival.
 
• Goga Navami falls on the **ninth day** of the Krishna Paksha (waning phase of the moon) in the month of **Bhadrapada** as per the Hindu calendar.
 
• People from various communities participate in the festival, highlighting its cultural significance.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated during the spring season in Jharkhand when sal trees wear new leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Sarhul**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sarhul festival, the most popular tribal celebration across the Jharkhand region, was celebrated on 4 April 2022.
 
• Sarhul means **worshipping trees**. It is celebrated during the spring season when the saal trees wear new leaves
 
• It is celebrated by the tribal communities of the local Sarna religion, most notably by the Munda, Ho, and Oraon tribes.
 
• It is celebrated at the beginning of spring every year in the first month of the Hindu calendar, on the third day of the moon or the fortnight of **‘Chaitra’**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The unmarried tribal girls celebrate the Jawa festival, which has its own kind of song and dance.

 
 
• This is held mainly for the expectation of good fertility and a better household.
 
 
 
• Sohrai is a harvest festival of the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
 
• It is also called the cattle festival.
 
 
 
• Karam is a harvest festival celebrated in the Indian states of Jharkhand, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Odisha and West Bengal.

questions.question: Losar (a new year festival) is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Losar **is a vibrant new year festival observed in **Arunachal Pradesh and Ladakh**, deeply rooted in Buddhist traditions.
 
• Occurring on the first day of the Tibetan lunar calendar, Losar heralds the arrival of spring and symbolizes the onset of new beginnings.
 
• Central to the festivities are rituals aimed at dispelling malevolent forces and invoking auspicious energies. Across regions like Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh, Losar unfolds over a 15-day period marked by fervent celebrations.
 
• Communities come together to adorn their homes, engage in religious observances, and prepare elaborate offerings for divine entities. In the spirit of hospitality, people welcome both kinfolk and strangers alike.
 
• Amidst the jubilant atmosphere, traditional delicacies like "kapse," a special type of cake, and "chang," a fermented alcoholic beverage, are savored with gusto, adding to the festive cheer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**, often referred to as the 'Dawn-Lit Mountain Province,' is a state nestled in the northeastern region of India. 
 
• Established on February 20, 1987, it emerged from the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) territory. The capital and largest town of Arunachal Pradesh is Itanagar. 
 
• This state shares its borders with the Indian states of Assam and Nagaland to the south, while its international boundaries extend to Bhutan in the west and Myanmar in the east. 
 
• Notably, Arunachal Pradesh also shares a disputed border of 1,129 km with China's Tibet Autonomous Region to the north, demarcated by the McMahon Line. 
 
• Although China claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of the Tibet Autonomous Region, its occupation of certain regions in 1962 was subsequently reversed.
